# Keywords

Words the language server explains on hover. The first group is Odin's; the second is what Vidar adds. All of Vidar's are contextual: they stay usable as ordinary names.

## Vidar keywords

### `catch`

Handles the error result of a statement: `x := f() catch err { ... }` (the block must leave the scope) or `f() catch unreachable`.

### `closure`

A closure type: `closure(params) -> results`. Any proc literal with a capture list `proc[a, &b]() { ... }` has one; plain procs convert to it.

### `errdefer`

A `defer` that only runs when the procedure returns a failure (a non-nil last result).

### `impl`

Binds procs to an interface's methods for a type: `impl Iface for Type { method = proc_name }`.

### `interface`

An interface: `Name :: interface { method, ... }` lists procs whose first parameter is `Name`. `interface { using Parent, ... }` extends another interface.

### `quote`

Inside a comptime proc, builds code: `quote(expr)` gives an `Expr`, `quote { stmts }` a `Stmt`. `$name` and `$(expr)` splice compile-time values in.

### `take`

Gives the value of a `do! { ... }` or `comptime! { ... }` block: `take x` (or `take a, b`).

### `unreachable`

Marks code that cannot run. `f() catch unreachable` panics if `f` fails.

## Odin keywords

### `asm`

Inline assembly.

### `auto_cast`

Converts to whatever type the context expects.

### `bit_field`

A struct whose fields are packed into bits of a backing integer.

### `bit_set`

A set of enum members or a range, stored as bits: `bit_set[Enum]`.

### `break`

Leaves the innermost loop or switch (or the labeled one).

### `case`

A branch of a `switch`; `case:` alone is the default branch.

### `cast`

Converts a value: `cast(T)x` (same as `T(x)`).

### `context`

```odin
context: runtime.Context
```

The implicit context passed to every Odin procedure: allocators, logger, user data. Assign to its fields to change them for the rest of the scope.

### `continue`

Jumps to the next iteration of the innermost loop.

### `defer`

Runs a statement when the enclosing scope exits.

### `distinct`

Makes a new type with the same layout as another but not interchangeable with it: `Id :: distinct int`.

### `do`

Introduces a one-statement body on the same line: `if x do return`.

### `dynamic`

A growable array: `[dynamic]T`. Grow with `append`, release with `delete`.

### `else`

The branch taken when the `if` condition is false; `a if cond else b` in a ternary.

### `enum`

An enumeration: `Name :: enum { A, B }`. Members are written `.A` where the type is known.

### `fallthrough`

Continues into the next `case` of a switch.

### `false`

```odin
false: untyped bool
```

Boolean false.

### `for`

Loop: `for cond { }`, `for i := 0; i < n; i += 1 { }`, `for x in xs { }`, `for i in 0..<n { }`.

### `foreign`

Declares a block of procedures from a foreign (C) library.

### `if`

Conditional: `if cond { ... } else { ... }`; `if x := f(); x > 0 { ... }` with an init statement.

### `import`

Imports a package: `import "core:fmt"`, `import alias "path"`. Vidar packages may import each other in cycles.

### `in`

Iterates in a `for` loop, binds the value in a type switch, or tests set membership: `x in set`.

### `map`

A hash map type: `map[Key]Value`. Create with `make(map[K]V)`, release with `delete`.

### `matrix`

A matrix type: `matrix[rows, cols]T`.

### `nil`

The zero value of pointers, maps, slices, dynamic arrays, procs, closures, interfaces, unions and `any`.

### `not_in`

Tests that a value is not in a `bit_set` or map.

### `or_break`

Breaks out of the enclosing loop when the last result is a failure.

### `or_continue`

Continues the enclosing loop when the last result is a failure.

### `or_else`

`x := f() or_else default`: the default when the last result of `f` is false, nil or an error.

### `or_return`

Returns early when the last result is a failure. Vidar adds `f() or_return .Err` to return a different error.

### `package`

Names the package this file belongs to. Every file in a directory must use the same name.

### `proc`

A procedure: `name :: proc(params) -> results { ... }`. `proc!` declares a comptime proc (a macro); `proc[captures]` a closure literal.

### `return`

Returns from the enclosing procedure. A bare `return` returns the named results.

### `struct`

A struct type: `Name :: struct { field: Type, ... }`.

### `switch`

Multi-way branch: `switch x { case 1: ... case: ... }`; `switch v in u { case T: ... }` for unions and `any`.

### `transmute`

Reinterprets the bits of a value as another type of the same size: `transmute(T)x`.

### `true`

```odin
true: untyped bool
```

Boolean true.

### `typeid`

```odin
typeid
```

The type of a type: a runtime id for any type.

### `union`

A tagged union type: `Name :: union { A, B }`. Inspect it with a type switch: `switch v in u { ... }`.

### `using`

Brings the fields of a struct (or the members of a package) into scope. In an interface, `using Parent` extends `Parent`.

### `when`

Compile-time `if`: only the taken branch is type checked and compiled.

### `where`

Constrains the parameters of a polymorphic procedure or struct.
